meta.title: Tihar House — a Nepali festival of lights
meta.description: A presentation-style journey through a Nepali home during Tihar: crows on the roof, dogs in the attic, lamps in the puja room, sel roti in the kitchen, and Bhai Tika in the garden.

intro.eyebrow: A journey through a Nepali home
intro.title: Tihar House
intro.subtitle: Five days. One house. Every lamp a welcome.
intro.note: Sound is off by default. Turn it on for the room tone.

roof.title: The roof, before sunrise.
roof.body: Tihar begins before the sun. On the thatched roof, the first diya is lit and food is left for the crows — kag, the birds said to carry messages to Yama. Mist drifts over the valley. The house is still asleep.

attic.title: The roof lifts. The house opens.
attic.body: The thatch divides and the attic appears: beams, dust, a carved window. A dog is honoured with a marigold garland and a good meal — a thank-you for loyalty, and for the guardian at Yama's gate. In 2026 this day shares the calendar with Laxmi Puja.

puja.title: The house fills with light.
puja.body: Cows are thanked in the morning. By evening the puja room glows: diyas on every ledge, marigold at the door, and Laxmi's footprints leading inward. The house is cleaned, lit, and left open for the goddess of wealth.
puja.note: Laxmi Puja 8 Nov · Gai Tihar 9 Nov

kitchen.title: The kitchen keeps the year.
kitchen.body: Firelight, copper, steam. Sel roti rings bubble in oil. On this day Newar families celebrate Mha Puja — the worship of the self — and many households honour Govardhan and the oxen that work the fields. Nepal Sambat begins.

doorway.title: The door opens to the garden.
doorway.body: The last day belongs to brothers and sisters. The carved door swings open onto evening air, where a rangoli is waiting and the tika tray is set. Walk through.

garden.title: A promise, drawn in colour.
garden.body: In the garden, the rangoli draws itself in powder and petals. Seven colours are layered on the tika. Border diyas are lit. Then the camera pulls back — the garden, the house, the whole valley glowing.
garden.final: The house is full of light.

guide.title: Quick Guide
guide.intro: The practical bits, without the theatre.

dates.source: Dates checked against Hamro Patro 2083 and Nepali Calendar 2083.

days.title: The five days
days.intro: A short guide to each day. Customs vary by family, caste, community and region — these are starting points, not a single rulebook.

items.name: Kag Tihar
items.body: Crows are fed on roofs and in the street at dawn. They are linked with Yama, the god of death, and are treated as messengers.
items.practice: Put out grains, seeds or a little rice before sunrise, somewhere safe from traffic.

items.name: Kukur Tihar
items.body: Dogs — pets, working dogs and strays — are honoured with garlands, tika and good food. The day thanks them for loyalty and protection.
items.practice: Offer clean water and dog-safe food. Ask before giving treats to a dog you do not know. Keep loud fireworks away from animals.

items.name: Gai Tihar & Laxmi Puja
items.body: Cows are honoured in the morning. In the evening, homes are cleaned and lit for Laxmi, the goddess of wealth. Diyas, garlands and rangoli mark the night.
items.practice: Light a diya at the door. Keep flames away from children, pets and curtains. Use LED diyas where a flame is not safe.

items.name: Govardhan Puja & Mha Puja
items.body: Newar families worship the self in Mha Puja and mark the start of Nepal Sambat. Many households honour Govardhan and the oxen.
items.practice: Share a meal. If you are Newar, follow your family's Mha Puja tradition. If you are not, this is a good day to learn about Nepal Sambat.

items.name: Bhai Tika
items.body: Sisters and brothers exchange tika, garlands, blessings and gifts. The seven-colour tika is a mark of protection and long life.
items.practice: Prepare a tray, a garland, a diya and a small gift. Ask your family about the order of the ritual before you improvise.

celebrate.title: How to celebrate
celebrate.intro: You do not need a full ritual to mark Tihar. Start with one lamp and one act of care.

items.title: Light one lamp
items.body: A single diya at the door is enough to begin. Clay, a cotton wick, oil. Keep it on a stable, heat-safe surface, away from curtains and pets.

items.title: Make a rangoli
items.body: Use rice flour, coloured powder, sand or petals. Start with a circle and build outward. The motif in this site is a placeholder, not a rule.

items.title: Feed the day's animal
items.body: Grains for crows, water and dog-safe food for dogs, fresh grass and treats for cows. Kindness is the point.

items.title: Clean and open the house
items.body: Tihar is a welcome. Clear the doorway, light the dark corners, and leave the door open for guests.

items.title: Sing, play, share
items.body: Deusi and Bhailo are sung door to door. Join respectfully, ask before filming, and give what you can.

items.title: Remember the animals
items.body: Fireworks frighten dogs and birds. Keep celebrations quiet around them, and never leave lit diyas where a tail can reach.

etiquette.title: If you are a visitor
items: Ask before you photograph a household's puja.
Take off your shoes where asked.
Do not touch the tika tray or offerings unless invited.
Give and receive with your right hand where that is customary.
Dates and customs vary by family, caste and region. Ask.

words.confirmBody: Every detail here has been confirmed with multiple Nepali families and checked against published Nepali calendars and cultural sources. Where households differ, we say so rather than guess.

guide.teaserBody: Dates, rituals and recipes in five short sections.
